recipes.name: Quick Weekday Pasta
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can reduced fat cream of chicken soup
2 cups chopped frozen broccoli, thawed and drained

steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Once the water is boiling, stir in the rotini, and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the pasta has cooked through, but is still firm to the bite, about 10 minutes. Drain well in a colander set in the sink.
Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In a bowl, mix soup, broccoli, chicken, and milk. Season with garlic powder and pepper. Transfer to a baking dish and top with Cheddar cheese.
Cover and bake 20 minutes in the preheated oven. Remove cover and continue baking 10 minutes, until bubbly.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Weekday Pasta
raw_recipe.description: This easy pasta dish is made with frozen broccoli, pre-cooked chicken, and canned soup for a quick, delicious weeknight meal.

review.reviewBody: I made this as a side dish, so I excluded the chicken and added a few more ounces of pasta. I also used canned green beans instead of the broccoli and added the cheese in with everything. I added italian seasoning as well. Topped the dish with seasoned breadcrumbs mixed with a little melted butter...I also added a little garlic to the breadcrumbs. We really enjoyed it! Super easy and will make again!

We really enjoyed this recipe. I followed advice of some of the other reviewers and added a couple of extra spices including increasing the garlic powder, adding 1 tsp of Italian seasoning, 1/2 tsp onion powder, 1 tsp smokehouse maple seasoning. Also melted 2 TBLS butter and mixed with Italian bread crumbs and sprinkled over the top along with some french fried onions. I added 1/2 c shredded cheese into mixture and 1/2 cup on the top of the casserole. We all enjoyed this. I like that it is a recipe that you can make your own based on your family's tastes.

Made alot of adjustments. Used Broccoli Cheese soup instead (didn't have Cream of Chicken on hand), added about 1/2 cup leftover cooked Quinoa, about 3/4 cup leftover cooked sprouted bean trio, 1/2 sliced cooked mushrooms and more spices. Used about 1 tsp. pepper, about 1 tsp. of garlic powder and threw in Tony Chachere's seasoning to taste-about 1/2 tsp. or more. Because of the added protein of Quinoa and beans, I only added half of the cooked noodles the original recipe called for. Put in baking dish, sprinkled with plain bread crumbs and then sprayed bitter flavored cooking spray over the crumbs (it's all about cutting unnecessary fat). Mo need gor added chefdar cheese (again citting the fat). Baked as recommended. Eating it now and it tastes pretty pretty good!
I had fresh broccoli so I blanched it in the pasta pot prior to dropping the noodles i had. I also added fresh mushrooms and chopped pimentos. Very good week day supper.

I doubled the recipe.
Used one can cream of chicken, one can cream of mushroom
Added: 1 cup sour cream, 1 tsp paprika, 1/2 cup mini peppers (sauteed), about 1/2 cup grated Italian blend cheese to the mixture
Topped with colby jack grated cheese and paprika, baked for 20 mins, then added crunchy onions to the top and baked for additional 10 mins.

Just needed a bit of salt to make it perfect. Bonus - kids loved it.

We reeeeally liked this one. It really hit the spot. I did change a couple things: I added 1/4 cup more milk, 1/2 tsp more pepper and 1/2 tsp more garlic powder; not because it needed them, but only because we like the extra pepper & garlic flavors. I also mixed melted butter with seasoned bread crumbs and sprinkled it on top. Came out awesome! Definately going on our "regulars" list........Michelle
This recipe was great. The only thing that I did differently was use 1 cup shredded cheese (mixed half cup into the pasta mixture and sprinkled the other half cup onto the top).

So yummy! I modified a bit. I added some sour cream, Cayenne, Paprika, and I topped with crushed Ritz crackers. I also mixed the cheese throughout and just added a little to the top along with the crumbs. It was so simple! I will definitely make it again with my small changes

LOVED this! I addend onion, green peppers and diced tomatoes. I also sprinkled dried crushed hot peppers over the top of the chicken, to make it a bit spicy, useda mix of mozzarella and colby cheese and topped it all of with breadcrumb/butter mixture. It was AWESOME! Next time I will also top with black olives and serve with sour cream.... Thank you for sharing this delicious recipe
This is very quick and easy. I made it with double the noodles and just added little extra milk. I also mixed unseasoned breadcrumbs with melted butter and sprinkled on top for a little crispiness.
Quick and a hit with the kids! I doubled this recipe and filled a 13x9 pan. I added approx 3/4 cup of sour cream and topped with a combo of melted butter mixed with a 1/2 sleeve of ritz crackers.
There was not enough flavor or as I always say, it needed a “punch”..I might try putting shredded cheese in the mix as well as on top…For my family, I also need to make 2 receipts…
I used ham leftovers from Easter and it was delicious!

I made this per the instructions. It lacked flavor all-around. I did not like it. There are so many other recipes similar to this one that I won`t try to figure out how to make this so that I like it.
my kids didnt like
quick, easy
I added some salt and onion powder to the mix. I accidentally added the 1/2 cup of cheese to the mix then topped it with more cheese. I liked it. My 2 year old loved it.
I used 2% evaporated milk, switched spinach for broccoli and doubled the amount of chicken and noodles. It was great!!
I used left-over cajun chicken. This was okay. A little boring but quick and easy.
As written, this is very bland. On that note, it is a great starter recipe to add ingredients according to your family's tastes.
